questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my spanish and Colombia is an incredible country, which I wanted to get to know better

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's "easy" to do an exchange at Uniandes (Bogotá) because they are so used to having exchange students, so they are super good at helping with whatever question you might have. I love Colombia. The reason why it's not a 10 is just that Bogotá is a super intense city and the uni is located in a rather unsafe area, but if just don't walk alone at night and then you will be fine:)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Rather easy, the Uni in Colombia is quick to answer questions over e-mail, but I mostly asked my friend who had done an exchange there before, who helped me a lot - so if you need assistance just ask in the "KU South America" facebook group if you can talk to someone who has been at the destination you're going to

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is an exchange office at Uniandes which I visited frecuently in the beginning of my stay, especially in the course selection period

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in a student house which I got recommended by my friend who had lived there before, there are lots in Bogotá, especially in La Candelaria (area close to uni) - write in the Facebook group for KU students in South America for recommendations (I can't write the whatsapp numbers for accommodation here...)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's fun to share a house with other people! But in La Candelaria (or generally in the center of Bogotá) I would not walk around at night... Take an uber or indrive when you're going somewhere when it's dark

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you're living on campus I would recommend "Central X" and try to find roomies in the exchange group to share an apartment with.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You can get help from the exchange office at uni and also they do a turtorial for exchange students the day of the course selection, so you're in good hands

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Go to the "help with course registration" event for exchange students that they host the day of course selections. They did the registration for me!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The people from the exchange office walked around and helped the exchange students to choose courses in their online registration program

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Exchange students can choose courses first so it went easy for me, I had 30 "free" ECTS which also helped. If you have problems go as soon as possible to the exchange office so they can help you

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a super nice Uni to have "free" ECTS points at because they have a big sports center so you can also get ECTS points for participating in sports!! And they have a summer spanish course (free for exchange students) which you can transfer ECTS for, would highly reccommend doing that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It's the most expensive uni in Colombia (maybe south america) so crazy good facilities. The students are in general super young though and a bit boring, but the teaching is good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I did a lot of courses I can't do at UCPH, like arts and sports, so very nice to have the opportunity to try subjects that is not part of your usual carreer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Colombia (espacio, tiempo, diferencia), Salsa & Bachata, Spanish course level 2 & 3, Dibujo basicó

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do sports courses and art classes:)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The everyday life is not that expensive, you can buy nice ok cheap lunch close to uni. The expensive costs are the weekend trips (not super expensive to travel in bus, but if you do it a lot with friends it always adds up!)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general a nice and cheap everyday life

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Incredible quite american inspired sports center!! They have a swimming pool you can use for free!!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sports you can think off! Take dance classes !!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on a lot of weekend trips (in bus ofc;) - try to plan your subjects so you don't have classes monday or friday (or both) so you have long weekends to do stuff!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The pacific coast (also the carribbean - but the pacific is extraordinary) - you can see whales there! The area around Salento (the national park Sierra Nevada), 3-day hike in Santander (Camino Real hedder selve hiken), visit the Amazonas !!! (Leticia - from Leticia go to Puerto Nariño and take a 4-day slow boat to Iquitos in Peru). Visit "los llanos" region (western-vibe region east for Bogota), Caribbean coast (Minka and Tayrona nacional Park)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Colombian people are the sweetest and most welcoming, love to party and chat, also if you don't know a lot of spanish

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't worry if you don't make a lot of friends at Uniandes, the people studying there are super young and rich, you can find friends outside. Go to "La Casa de la Paz" in Chapinero area, very sweet people there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Difference in time management, you have to check in some times if you meet up with a colombian person to know if it's actually happening and a lot of people cancel on the day haha

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone loves to dance, to talk and to get to know you. Super heart warming, curious and welcoming people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Take sports classes or art classes
2) plan your schedule so you have multiple days off
3) remember that it's the most expensive univeristy in Colombia so people going there are just more reserved
4) Eat lunch at "mi Caserito" close to uni!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Don't panic regarding Bogotá. I never fell in love with that city due to it's super intense traffic and not a lot of green areas, but all other parts of Colombia are incredible. Watch out at night though in Bogotá, especially in the center, always take a Uber or Indrive home (also don't trust regular cab drivers). Bring an extra phone just in case it gets stolen.
AND don't (!!!) tell Folkeregisteret that you're away. If you're away for more than 6 months they cancel you from Folkeregisteret (so you can't vote in elections and you just receive a lot of stuff in your e-boks). Move your adress to your parents and register yourself as on exchange in
SU.dk
, then everything is fine:)
Uh and also visit "Parque Entre Nubes" in Bogotá, very beautiful place in the southern part of the city.
The food in general in the country is not super good, they choose not to use spices, but they have the best fruits and juices. Good vegetarian food at "Maria Candela" in bogotá.
Bring sunscreen and vitamins from home (good sunscreen is expensive to buy).
If you're going on weekend trips try to book your bus late (after 21) - the traffic is super dense so you will arrive at the same time

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my spanish, getting to know a beautiful country and getting a lot of good friends to visit in Europe (from exchange)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accepting that learning a language takes super long time but that you're improving each day also without knowing it:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
